title: Permission tests must grant one exact action, not blanket true/false
answers: How should I write a test for an RBAC permission check?
Why did my permission check regression slip through tests?
body: Convention enforced by review on this PR: tests for RBAC-gated helpers must not stub contextSrv.hasPermission to always return true/false (that passes even if the code checks the wrong action, e.g. a revert from notebooks:create back to notebooks:write or dashboards:create). Instead grant the exact single action under test, assert the check passes, then grant every other related action except it and assert the check fails. See public/app/features/notebook/permissions.test.ts and public/app/features/notebook/mutation-api/commands/permissions.test.ts for the pattern (a `grant(...actions)` helper mocking hasPermission against an explicit allow-list).
applies: Unit tests for any contextSrv.hasPermission-based gating logic in the frontend
